title: The Last Page of the Notebook
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：account　|　正文 381 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 account 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: My mother kept the accounts in a grey notebook: rent, food, bus fares, everything. She checked them every evening by the window. On the first page she opened a small ① account for me when I was ten, with my name written in pencil. Every month she wrote down what I had spent and what I had saved, and she never once did it without asking me to sit beside her.

I did not love those evenings. She would read out each line, then give me a clear ② account of where the money had gone: bus fares, a notebook, the cake I could not resist. Rent and food together ③ accounted for almost two thirds of everything she earned, and seeing that ④ accounted for why she always said no to the things I wanted most.

When I turned sixteen she said I could manage one hundred yuan a month myself. 'But you must ⑤ take account of the small things,' she warned. 'The bus, the water, the pen you lose every week.' She even agreed that my marks might improve ⑥ on account of fewer arguments about money, and she laughed when she said it.

Last winter she lost her job for three months. I offered to give her my savings. She refused, and I could see from her face that this was not the moment to argue; the notebook stayed shut. What she did instead was keep two ⑦ accounts in the same notebook, one for her savings and one for mine, so that the two sums would never be mixed. Slowly I came to see how much wisdom there was in that grey book.

Now I keep my own book, though mine is on a phone, with one page for food and one for books. I write down every purchase before I forget it, and ⑧ on no account do I write a sum I am not sure about. At the end of each month I look at the last page and try to give myself an honest ⑨ account of the thirty days. It is rarely flattering. Every account has a last page, and the last page never lies. But ⑩ by all accounts my mother's method has done for me what no lecture on wealth ever could: it taught me to look before I spend.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 描述；叙述；说明
D. v. 解释；说明（account for）
E. 固定搭配：take account of 把……考虑在内
F. 固定搭配：on account of 因为；由于
G. 固定搭配：on no account 决不（句首倒装）
H. 固定搭配：by all accounts 据说；据大家说

items.q: she opened a small account for me
give me a clear account of where the money had gone
Rent and food together accounted for almost two thirds
and seeing that accounted for why she always said no
you must take account of the small things
on account of fewer arguments about money
keep two accounts in the same notebook
on no account do I write a sum
give myself an honest account of the thirty days
by all accounts my mother's method

answers.why: open an account 是开设账户，宾语是账户，后文说写着我的名字，取名词“账户”。
give sb an account of＋内容，意为“把经过叙述／说明给某人听”，此处是把钱的去向说清楚。
account for＋比例，是动词短语“（数量上）占”，房租和食物占了收入的三分之二。
account for＋why 从句，是另一义：解释、说明原因，说明母亲总是拒绝的原因。
take account of sth 意为“考虑到某事”，母亲提醒我把零碎开支也算进去。
on account of＋名词，意为“因为”，这里是说因为少了争吵，成绩或许会好些。
keep accounts 是名词复数“账目、账簿”，此处指母亲把两笔钱分两本账记，以免混淆。
on no account 意为“决不”，置于句首时主谓部分倒装（do I write），是强调的否定。
give sb an account of＋对象，与第 2 题同义，意为“对这三十天做个如实交代”。
by all accounts 位于句首，意为“据说、大家都这么说”，用来总结母亲方法的效果。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 母亲在我十岁那年给我开了一个账户。（account）
她每月都把钱的去向对我说明一遍。（give an account of）
房租和食物占她收入的三分之二。（account for）
你必须把那些零碎开支也考虑进去。（take account of）
因为少了关于钱的争吵，我的成绩提高了。（on account of）
我决不写下自己没有把握的数字。（on no account）
answers: My mother opened a small account for me when I was ten.
Every month she gave me a clear account of where the money had gone.
Rent and food accounted for two thirds of her income.
You must take account of the small everyday expenses as well.
My marks improved on account of fewer arguments about money.
On no account do I write down a sum I am not sure about.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 account 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: The day my mother opened an account for me, she also gave me a grey notebook of my own.
Every month she gave me a clear account of where every yuan of her income had gone.
Rent and food accounted for almost two thirds of it, which explained why she rarely bought new clothes.
Before I spend anything I now take account of the small things, such as bus fares and lost pens.
On no account do I borrow from friends, because no debt is easier to pay than none.
By all accounts this simple habit teaches young people more about money than any lecture on wealth.
